objective: Produce a compact, mechanism-preserving BBB auxiliary ontology without imposing a fixed vocabulary size.

namespace_policy.rule: Every decision applies to exactly one source/output namespace. Similar labels in another namespace require a separate decision and may remain different.

context.rule: Keep the shortest label that preserves every explicit decision-relevant dimension; do not merge mechanistically distinct contexts merely to reduce vocabulary size.

species.default_form: Concise lowercase explicit species labels; deduplicate, alphabetize, and join multiple species with ' + '.
species.role_qualification_rule: Use host/gene role qualification only when the raw source explicitly states both the expression host species and the introduced gene species.
species.single_role_rule: When both roles are not explicit, do not invent a role assignment; retain only species that are independently explicit under the namespace source contract.

merge.meaning: Map two or more semantically equivalent provisional labels to one canonical label within the same namespace.

rename.meaning: Replace one provisional label with a clearer canonical label without changing its covered raw values.

split.meaning: Divide one provisional label into two or more final labels using explicit raw-value assignments.
requirements: Every affected raw value is assigned exactly once.
Selectors or raw-value lists are explicit, deterministic, exhaustive, and non-overlapping.
Each child label has supporting raw examples and an independent rationale.
The split does not infer information absent from the raw source.

evidence_requirements: Evidence quotes or examples come from raw values in the same namespace.
Merge and rename decisions show representative examples for every input label.
Split decisions identify all affected raw values and examples for every child label.
Rationale states why preserved ontology dimensions are equivalent or different.

review_workflow.reviewer: Proposes retain, merge, rename, or split decisions with complete evidence and rationale.
review_workflow.checker: Independently checks source support, namespace scope, ontology preservation, and raw-value coverage.
review_workflow.adjudicator: Resolves reviewer/checker disagreement and accepts or rejects each proposed change; the adjudicator may not silently rewrite a decision without a new rationale.
review_workflow.human_publication_checkpoint: A human must approve the final manifest, unresolved-item report, and change summary before the reconciled mapping is published or used to rebuild downstream artifacts.
publication_requires: All reviewed inputs have an explicit disposition.
All accepted changes have checker and adjudicator identities.
All splits pass exhaustive and non-overlapping raw-value coverage checks.
No forbidden cross-namespace decision is present.
No unresolved reviewer/checker disagreement is present.

forbidden_decisions: Any merge, rename, or split spanning more than one source/output namespace.
Any decision that transfers a context label into a species namespace or a species label into a context namespace.
Any merge that removes an explicit assay/model type, in vivo/in vitro setting, transport mechanism or direction, barrier-disruption state, or major BBB modality.
Any label based on compound, target, dose, time, pathogen, clone, or protocol detail when that detail is not essential to a preserved ontology dimension.
Any species or host/gene role inferred from a model name, cell line, gene symbol, transporter name, assay abbreviation, or outside knowledge.
Any vocabulary-size target used as justification for a semantic merge.
Any unreviewed automatic change to the published mapping.
